# COP31 ends without an overarching climate deal after fossil-fuel dispute

**Desk:** India & World Briefs  
**Location:** Antalya, Türkiye  
**Updated:** 22 November 2026, 20:00 IST  
**Status:** Verified brief draft; held for the next eligible publication window  
**Proposed URL:** https://vridhi.ink/journal/cop31-ends-without-overarching-climate-deal/

The UN climate conference in Antalya ended on Sunday, 22 November, without consensus on an overarching political decision, after negotiations ran nearly 48 hours beyond their scheduled finish. Reuters and the Associated Press reported that the proposed Turkish–Australian text did not explicitly mention fossil fuels, prompting the European Union and several other parties to reject it. Smaller decisions and initiatives continued, so the summit did not end with every workstream producing nothing.

## What is confirmed

COP31 President Murat Kurum told Reuters that no new text would be prepared without consensus and that existing decisions would be implemented. Negotiations president Chris Bowen said parties had been unable to agree on a cover decision. AP independently reported that the talks ended without that overarching agreement.

The central dispute concerned whether the final text should explicitly refer to moving away from fossil fuels. Climate finance, carbon capture and the response to projected warming beyond the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C threshold were also contested.

## India's stated position

In its official opening statement on 10 November, India called for equity and the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities. It highlighted adaptation and just-transition challenges for developing countries and said public finance from developed countries remained central, citing their obligations under Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement. This was India's opening position—not a post-summit reaction.

## What remains unresolved

The overarching cover decision was not adopted. The precise status and text of individual agenda decisions should be checked against the official UNFCCC record when closing documentation is posted. At the time of this draft, the UNFCCC conference page still showed updates through 20 November and no closing-outcome summary. This brief does not claim that every agenda item failed or that existing Paris Agreement commitments were cancelled.

## Why it matters

For countries managing climate impacts while pursuing development, fossil-fuel transition, adaptation finance and access to technology are practical questions, not just negotiating language. India's stated emphasis on equity, adaptation and finance helps explain why the balance between climate ambition and support matters to the Global South.
